newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melbourne may have merger to announce.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melbourne may have merger to announce.

text.p: Bank of Melbourne Ltd, a high profile regional bank which has been eyed by its bigger rivals, could be preparing the share market for a merger deal, perhaps from a foreign bank, analysts said.

The bank on Wednesday sought a share trading halt ahead of an announcement tomorrow about what it called "a confidential proposal, the terms of which have not been concluded". Its shares also soared in local trade.
Analysts said Westpac Banking Corp, one of Australia's big four banks, or St George Bank Ltd were the most likely bidders -- if that was the intention of the statement to the stock exchange.
But most also noted that the political and regulatory climate was not conducive to a takeover bid at the moment.

"There might be market speculation on this but let's face it they can speculate all they like, the Treasurer's hosed it down and it's got to go through the ACCC (Australian Competition and Consumer Commission)," ANZ Securities bank analyst Greg Tucker said. The ACCC is the nation's anti-monopolies watchdog and has
had to be convinced about the wisdom and benefits of some earlier industry couplings.
Before the announcement, the bank's shares jumped 65 cents to A$8.80, valuing the company at A$1.166 billion.
Westpac shares finished the day down 23.7 cents to A$6.873, reviving market speculation that it was Bank of Melbourne's suitor.
"Westpac's the mooted buyer and is looking to take out Bank of Melbourne which has been speculated for up for two years," said one analyst who declined to be named.
Burdett Buckeridge and Young senior dealer Stephen Smith said: "I think the market's a bit sort of edgy, thinking that Westpac will make a bid. It seems to be a reasonable fit."
However, the weakness in the Westpac share price was more due to the sale of 15 million shares by property and financial services group Lend Lease Corp.

Treasurer Peter Costello, who must approve any bank merger, said last week that he did not expect any merger application while the goverment was still considering the findings of the official Wallis Inquiry into the financial system.
Costello is due to release the Wallis report next week. The report is widely expected to recommend the relaxation of big bank merger rules.
The ACCC has said it would not allow a bank merger that left a state banking market without at least one regional bank, which specialise in home loans and small-medium corporate business.
J.B. Were & Son analyst Leigh Cronins said the absence of a trading halt on another listed Australian bank meant a bid might be from an offshore player.
"Obviously everyone's thinking that some sort of takeover is going to be announced but whether it's going to be an Australian bank or an overseas bank we don't really know," Cronins said.
"You might have thought that if it was an Australian bank that there might have been a trading halt applied to another bank."
Bank of Melbourne is Victoria's only large regional bank.
Its last chief executive, David Airey, resigned in January and has yet to be replaced.
-- Melbourne bureau 61-3 9826-1435
